claims.text: Adding a controlled dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature mechanical performance relative to the alloy without oxide dispersion.
Adding Y2O3 nanoparticles will preserve the alloy's thermal stability.
Adding Y2O3 nanoparticles will preserve the alloy's irradiation stability.
The initial conventionally fabricated MoNbTaW-based refractory high-entropy alloy has a homogeneous microstructure without oxide dispersion.
Premixing Y2O3 nanopowder with alloy powder followed by consolidation can produce a uniform oxide dispersion in the alloy matrix.
The dispersed Y2O3 nanoprecipitates will remain thermally stable under the proposed service conditions.
Uniformly distributed Y2O3 nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion.
Uniformly distributed Y2O3 nanoprecipitates hinder grain-boundary sliding.
Y2O3 nanoparticles inhibit the nucleation of defects generated during high-temperature deformation and irradiation.
Y2O3 nanoparticles inhibit the propagation of defects generated during high-temperature deformation and irradiation.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles resist coarsening or dissolution under service conditions.
Resistance of the nanoparticles to coarsening or dissolution maintains the alloy's microstructural integrity and mechanical strength.
The Y2O3-reinforced alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the oxide-free baseline.
The Y2O3-reinforced alloy will have greater creep resistance than the oxide-free baseline.
A nonuniform nanoparticle distribution may compromise ductility or induce unwanted phase changes.
An excessive Y2O3 volume fraction may compromise ductility or induce unwanted phase changes.
